lines.text: What if you just... stopped sleeping?
Night one. You feel fine. Kind of wired. But after twenty-four hours awake, your brain works like it's legally drunk.
Day two. Your brain starts taking micro-naps. A few seconds asleep, with your eyes open, and you don't even notice.
Day three. Things move in the corner of your eye. The walls seem to breathe. You start to hallucinate.
In nineteen sixty-four, a high school student named Randy Gardner tried this. He stayed awake for eleven days. A world record.
By the end, he couldn't remember simple words, couldn't finish a sentence, and saw things that weren't there.
And in lab experiments, rats kept awake for about two to three weeks... died.
Sleep is when your brain takes out the trash. Skip it, and the trash piles up.
So, be honest. How many hours did you sleep last night?
